Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Per-query parked-output bookkeeping in the CN. Findings to read: B4 (and B1 for the dispatch order). Code to read: engine.rs ParkedOutput/park/drop_parked/Err path; compute_node_service.rs dispatch worker, cancel_plan_fragment, run_ready_fragment; local_exchange.rs take_ready and removal; result_store.rs query_failures; what the FE sends on failure and cancel.
Angle: the design a senior engineer would ship for the long run: correct under cancellation and concurrency, observable (log/telemetry), configurable where it must be, with the failure modes enumerated.
Produce ONE complete design: mechanism (what changes, in which functions, how it behaves under the measured SF1000 case and under the 15 passing queries), files to touch, tests (unit/component and the SF1000 acceptance), predicted effect with numbers derived from the evidence, risks, effort, dependencies on the other three fixes. Write your full design as markdown to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/parked-bookkeeping-robust.md (include the code excerpts you relied on with file:line) and return the structured summary.

Use when choosing GPU_MEM, STAGING, HOST_MEM, hash_partition_bytes, scan_task_batch_size, or when a query OOMs / exhausts the exchange arena / looks like an engine bug that is actually mis-sizing. Covers the derived-flag path vs a full sirius.yaml.

- log-analyzer: Use this skill to analyze Sirius query execution logs — to find why a query is slow, diagnose validation errors (wrong results), spot excessive downgrading, identify pipeline gaps, or compare two runs of the same query. Trigger whenever the user mentions a Sirius log file, says "look at this log", asks about per-operator time, pipeline gaps, memory pressure, downgrade behavior, validation/correctness mismatches, or wants to compare two query runs. Also use as a hand-off target from race-check (for two-run comparisons), runtime-errors (for "where did the query stall before hang"), and validate (for diffing the bad run against a good run). This is the log-only counterpart to profile-analyzer (nsys) and optimization-advisor (source-level guidance).

Use PROACTIVELY before implementing features, fixing bugs, or writing new operators — analyzes the task description and loads cudf, rmm, duckdb, cucascade module docs to improve code quality. Trigger when the user asks to implement, add, fix, or modify GPU operators, pipeline components, memory management, joins, aggregations, sorting, expressions, or data I/O.
- module-discover: Discover and document a dependency library or submodule — analyzes all uses within the codebase, divides the library into logical modules, identifies which modules are used, and generates LLM-consumable API documentation for each module. Use when the user wants to understand a library dependency, map its modules, or generate API reference docs for a submodule.
- optimization-advisor: Use this skill to find exactly which source code to optimize for better GPU performance. Maps nsys profile hotspots to specific Sirius source files and functions, classifies bottlenecks as GPU-bound, CPU-bound, or sync-bound, and recommends actionable code changes. Trigger when the user wants to know what to optimize, where to focus coding effort, or wants source-level optimization guidance. This skill focuses on actionable source code targets — for generating performance reports and measurements, use profile-analyzer instead.

Use this whenever the user shares a GitHub PR URL (e.g. github.com/owner/repo/pull/1234) and wants to understand, summarize, review, walk through, or get up to speed on what changed — phrases like "can you review this PR", "what does this PR do", "help me understand this pull request", "summarize the changes in PR

1	# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them
2	
3	Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
4	(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
5	Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
6	one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
7	Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.
8	
9	## The four issues
10	
11	| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
12	|---|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
14	| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
15	| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
16	| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |
17	
18	## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)
19	
20	1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
21	2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
22	3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
23	4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.
24	
25	## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)
26	
27	1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
28	2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
29	3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
30	4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
31	5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.
32	
33	## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")
34	
35	| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
38	| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
39	| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
40	| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |
41	
42	## Workflows
43	
44	**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.
45	
46	**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.
47	
48	**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.
49	
50	## Status log
51	- 15:20 UTC: worktrees `fix-oom-failfast`, `fix-parked-bookkeeping`, `fix-files-cardinality`, `fix-fragment-fusion` being created and built; design workflow launched.

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).
16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.
20. DONE q15 determinism A/B on 1 CN (6 runs each): SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1 -> rows per run ['0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0'] (ms ['10331', '5161', '5182', '5002', '4876', '4809']); gate off -> rows ['0', '0', '1', '0', '0', '0'] (ms ['10576', '4795', '4847', '4799', '4661', '4788']). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).
21. CORRECTION to fact 6: the A/B in fact 20 REFUTES the simple hypothesis that the SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS gate alone explains q15's empty runs: with the canonical sort ON, 4 of 6 runs still return 0 rows (gate off: 5 of 6). The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. Standalone Sirius keeps DECIMAL and returns the row every time. Treat this as a correctness finding about equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; verify from cn1-canon-q15/ and cn1-nocanon-q15/ logs (declared cardinalities of streams 18/22 per run) and the translator's decimal->FP64 lowering (#1236, cast_to_fp64 in expr_translator.rs).

2	
3	Audience: Sirius engineers. Evidence root: `scratchpad/perf/sf1000` (paths below are relative to it unless they start with `src/`, `experimental/`, `duckdb/`, `cucascade/`, which are relative to the source worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf`). 4

Line numbers for the load-bearing source citations (StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676, gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348/409, streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112, node_translator.rs:1743-1762, compute_node_service.rs:468, engine.rs:278-280, exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248, HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127) were re-checked against the worktree at `45dab3be` while writing this report.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Setup
10	
11	### Build and data
12	
13	| item | value |
14	|---|---|
15	| worktree | `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf`, branch `perf/profile-sf1000` = `d24f02c4` + `85658f09` (aggregate gate) + `9a5a4da6` (async sender dispatch) + `45dab3be` (Quent probes: scan reads, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels) |
16	| data | `/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000`, decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table; lineitem 5,999,989,709 rows in 60 files (166 GiB on GPFS), orders 1.5e9, partsupp 8e8, customer 1.5e8, part 2e8, supplier 1e7 (parquet footers, agent-notes/planning-contrast.md) |
17	| storage | `/scratch` is GPFS; the uring datasource opens files `O_RDONLY|O_DIRECT` (`src/io/uring/uring_reactor.cpp:528`, `src/include/io/uring/config.hpp:27-28`), so warm runs re-read from GPFS, not the page cache |
18	| queries | `experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql`; every file declares all 8 tables as `WITH ... FILES()` CTEs |
19	| oracle | DuckDB CPU answers in `../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv`, compared at rel tol 1e-6 |
20	
21	### Arms
22	
23	| arm | what ran | configuration |
24	|---|---|---|
25	| `cn1` | StarRocks FE + 1 Sirius CN, all 22 queries | `GPU_MEM=100GiB HOST_MEM=160GiB STAGING=16GiB SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES=16GiB SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS=300 SIRIUS_CN_ENABLE_QUENT=1 SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` (capture-cn.sh:11-12); fragment dumps on (`SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS`); executor pipeline pool 4 threads (default, docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94) |
26	| `cn4` | FE + 4 CNs (one per GPU), the 15 queries that passed on `cn1` | same |
27	| `standalone` | DuckDB + Sirius extension in-process on GPU 0, same 15 queries | `sirius-standalone-quent.yaml`: usage_limit 100 GiB, host 160 GiB; DuckDB planner with parquet statistics; measured in-process by `standalone_run_labeled.py` |

30	
31	Each query ran once cold then twice warm; `results.md` reports the warm median (n=2). `run-queries.sh:19` stops a query after a failing cold run, so failed queries have one run. CN client timing is a `mysql` process per run (`run-queries.sh`), which adds 17-57 ms of process spawn and a failing `select @@version_comment limit 1` handshake statement per run (measured: FE AuditLog Time vs client wall, cn1 q11.r1 951 vs 969 ms, cn4 q11.r1 606 vs 663 ms). Standalone timing is in-process (9-22 ms outside the engine span).
32	
33	FE-side plans for all 22 queries were captured with 1 CN alive (`survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt`, `survey/plan-summary.txt`) and with 4 CNs alive (`survey/explain4/`, `survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt`). During the 1-CN survey the FE still had four CNs registered with three dead (survey/cluster.log ids 10001, 11001, 12002, 12003), which matters for one cost-model term (section 3A, finding P3).
34	
35	### How "supported" was decided
36	
37	A query is "supported on the CN path at SF1000" if the cold run on `cn1` returned rows without error. The 4-CN arm ran only those. Nothing was excluded a priori.

39	| outcome | queries | reason (measured) |
40	|---|---|---|

176	**Mechanism, corrected by the source skeptic.** The cited term `CostModel.visitPhysicalDistribution` BROADCAST = `outputSize * aliveBackendNumber` (`CostModel.java:419-424`) is inert in this deployment: the Sirius CNs register as COMPUTE NODEs (`experimental/starrocks/src/lib.rs:210-212` `ALTER SYSTEM ADD COMPUTE NODE`; cn4/cluster.log:201 `run_mode is shared_data`), and `ctx.getAliveBackendNumber()` counts only BACKENDs (`system/SystemInfoService.java:1047`), so it is 0. The node count enters through `HashJoinCostModel.getMemCost` (`sql/optimizer/cost/HashJoinCostModel.java:115-127`: `beNum = max(1, aliveBackendNumber + aliveComputeNodeNumber)` in shared-data mode, `memCost = rightOutput * beNum` for BROADCAST, weight 2 in `CostModel.getRealCost`). With every child at 1 row, `Statistics.getOutputSize` is the sum of projected type widths, and the rule reduces to: broadcast the right side iff its row width is below roughly the left width at 1 CN, and below roughly a quarter of it at 4 CNs. This reproduces every observed decision (q03: build 16 B vs probe 24 B -> BROADCAST at 1 CN, PARTITIONED at 4; customer 4 B vs orders 20 B -> BROADCAST at both; the survivors q22 `o_custkey` 4 B, q07 `c_custkey+c_nationkey`, q02 `ps_partkey+min` are the narrow ones). `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` (`task/EnforceAndCostTask.java:281-325`) never fires because it needs `rightChildStats.getOutputRowCount() > 15,000,000` (`SessionVariable.java:1833`).
177	
178	**What a row-count-only fix would and would not do (inference, hand computation of the FE cost code, medium confidence).** Giving FILES() scans a row count but leaving column stats UNKNOWN makes the FE estimate a join output as `max(L, R)` and range predicates at 0.5, so orders x customer in q03 is estimated at 375M-750M rows. That *arms* `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` against the broadcast the finding wants: broadcast is rejected when the right side is > 15M rows and the left is less than 10x its bytes (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:324-325`). Result: q12 and q19 flip to BROADCAST (saving ~26 GB), q03 and q10's customer join stay PARTITIONED, q14 stays a wash. Getting the q03/q10 plans additionally requires raising `broadcast_row_limit` / `broadcast_right_table_scale_factor` (`SessionVariable.java:1833-1836`), or column statistics (NDV) for FILES(), or neutralising the probe-cache penalty in `HashJoinCostModel` (`BROADCAST_MAT_RATIO` 12 vs `SHUFFLE_MAX_RATIO` 3).
179	
180	**Existing levers.** SQL join hints `JOIN [BROADCAST|SHUFFLE]` are honoured (`sql/parser/AstBuilder.java:6567-6575`, `JoinHelper.java:344-349`), but the grammar accepts them only in explicit `JOIN ... ON` syntax, not the kit's comma joins, and a hint disables reorder/commutativity for that join. `broadcast_row_limit = 0` forces shuffle everywhere (`EnforceAndCostTask.java:312-314`), which would help q22/q07/q02 and hurt q03/q12/q19. `cbo_debug_alive_backend_number` (`SessionVariable.java:1823`) changes only the BE count and cannot reproduce the 1-CN plan at 4 CNs.
181	
182	Confidence: high on the flip and the byte inflation; medium on the corrected cost arithmetic (not executed in the FE).
183	
184	#### P4 (confirmed, impact narrowed). Every CN statement pays a fixed ~120-270 ms before the first fragment runs
185	
186	**Measured** (first `fragment run started` minus `runs.csv start_utc`, agent-notes/mfs3_decomp.py, warm runs): cn1 q02 195/189 ms, q11 233/227, q15 193/190, q22 199/136; cn4 q02 175/200, q11 262/257, q15 206/211, q22 118/155. All 15 passing queries pay it: 127-239 ms (cn1), 118-270 ms (cn4). The tail after the last fragment is 2-8 ms. Standalone pays 9-22 ms, measured in-process.
187	
188	Decomposition of cn1 q02.r1 (client start 13:03:24.267; cn1/cluster.log RPC spans):
189	
190	| phase | window | ms |
191	|---|---|---:|
192	| mysql process + handshake (`select @@version_comment limit 1`, planned as UNION_NODE and refused by the CN) | +0 .. +13 | 13 (18-57 across runs) |
193	| 8 `get_file_schema` RPCs, one per FILES() CTE in the WITH clause (5 of them for tables q02 never reads); lineitem call busy 28.3 ms + idle | +20 .. +93 | 73 (median across runs 104 cn1 / 114 cn4) |
194	| FE planning, no CN activity | +93 .. +147 | 54 |
195	| deploy: 13 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs in 6 topological levels, ~40 ms dead time after every multi-reply level | +150 .. +329 | first fragment runs at +194.6 |
196	
197	Sources: `TableFunctionTable.java:264 -> getFileSchema():688-712` (one RPC per FILES() reference, no cache); `experimental/starrocks/src/file_schema.rs:62-70` reads every footer serially (60 for lineitem) and deliberately ignores the FE's `schema_sample_file_count` = 2 (`file_schema.rs:52-58`, `TableFunctionTable.java:114`). Deploy waves are the per-level loop in `AllAtOnceExecutionSchedule.schedule` over `ExecutionDAG.getFragmentsInTopologicalOrderFromRoot()` (`qe/scheduler/dag/ExecutionDAG.java:195`), root first, so the leaf scans arrive in the last levels and the whole deploy sits on the critical path.
198	
199	**Corrections.** The head does not "cap the 4-CN speed-up": with it removed, engine-only speed-ups are q02 1.10x, q22 1.12x, q11 1.83x, q15 2.46x, so only q11 is materially affected. It is 28%/36%/9%/37% (q02/q11/q15/q22) of the gap to standalone, not the dominant reason. FE-side cost is ~215 ms (cn1) vs ~205 ms (cn4) for q11.r1 from the AuditLog, so it does not grow with CN count. The ~40 ms inter-level gaps appear only after levels with two or more replies on one connection and are most likely Nagle + delayed ACK on the CN's accepted sockets (no `set_nodelay` in `experimental/starrocks/src/brpc.rs`; only outgoing `prpc_client.rs:170`): inference, medium confidence, testable with `stream.set_nodelay(true)` at brpc.rs:114.
200	
201	**Proposed changes.** (1) `file_schema.rs`: honour `schema_sample_file_count` or read footers concurrently and memoize by (path, len, mtime): saves 60-110 ms per query, high confidence. (2) Set TCP_NODELAY on accepted CN sockets (brpc.rs): saves ~40 ms per multi-reply level if the inference holds. (3) For 1 CN, test `SET enable_single_node_schedule = true` (`SessionVariable.java:3337`; `Deployer.deployFragmentsForSingleNode` issues one `exec_batch_plan_fragments` RPC, which the CN implements at `compute_node_service.rs:424-450`); FILES() qualifies (`FileScanNode` is not in `ScanNode.isConnectorScanNode`). Collapsing levels FE-side for 4 CNs is unsafe as written because stage-2 fragments carry an `is_cached` descriptor table (`Deployer.java:247-251`) that the CN resolves from a per-query cache (`compute_node_service.rs:954-988`). (4) Bench-kit hygiene: emit only the CTEs a query uses (saves 3-6 of the 8 RPCs; does not fix real users). Confidence: (1) high, measured share; (2) medium, inference; (3) medium, code reading only, not exercised (section 5, item 11); (4) high, bench-only.
202	
203	#### P5 (not adversarially verified). Semi/anti join sides, CTE inlining, lost operator fusion, dropped dynamic filters
204	
205	These were analysed by one agent each and not refuted or confirmed by skeptics. Evidence is measured unless marked.
206	
207	- **Semi/anti build side (PC-4, SAJ-2, SAJ-3).** q04: `5:LEFT SEMI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=4:EXCHANGE<-lineitem` with 3,793,363,900 rows (card-compare-cn1.txt line 20); 30.82 GB of `l_orderkey` parked (cn1-quent.txt q04 `STREAMING_SINK in=30.82GB`) and 22.76 GB shuffled on 4 CNs. The engine flips it internally: cn1/engine-cn0.log q04 F00 `HASH_JOIN (id=6) type: RIGHT_SEMI`, build = orders scan, probe = lineitem stream, so 1-CN time is at parity (1850 vs 1896 ms); the cost is memory and exchange volume, not time. q22: `11:LEFT ANTI JOIN (BROADCAST) build=10:EXCHANGE<-orders` 1.5B rows to every CN; per-CN `HASH_JOIN(15)` 0.516 s on 4 CNs vs 0.588 s on 1 CN (cn4-quent.txt q22.r1, cn1 q22.r0), which is why q22 scales 1.13x. Standalone uses `RIGHT_DELIM_JOIN RIGHT_ANTI` with the customer keys as build (standalone/runs/q22.explain.txt). The FE has the commutation rule (`rule/transformation/JoinCommutativityRule.java:34-44` LEFT_SEMI<->RIGHT_SEMI, LEFT_ANTI<->RIGHT_ANTI) but at cardinality 1 it never pays. The translator refuses `RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN` (`node_translator.rs:1743-1762`: the match has no RIGHT_SEMI arm, `_ => UnsupportedPlanNode "hash join type is unsupported"`) although the Substrait consumer (`substrait/src/from_substrait.cpp:558-560`) and the engine (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:245,273`) support it. Proposed: add `TJoinOp::RIGHT_SEMI_JOIN => (JoinType::RightSemi, JoinOutput::Right)` plus a `JoinOutput::Right` arm; small, high confidence on feasibility.
208	- **Anti join emulation (SAJ-5).** `LEFT_ANTI_JOIN => (JoinType::Left, JoinOutput::LeftAnti)` at node_translator.rs:1749 is an outer join plus `IS NULL` filter because `from_substrait.cpp:540-570` lacks LEFT_ANTI/RIGHT_ANTI. Measured cost in q22: `HASH_JOIN(15) in=6.59GB` -> `FILTER(16) in=6.93GB` -> `PROJECTION(17) in=0.22GB` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 832d7f224fc8), i.e. ~97% of the join output is produced and discarded. Proposed: add the two cases to `SubstraitToDuckDB::TransformJoinOp` and map them natively (engine has `JoinType::ANTI`/`RIGHT_ANTI`, `sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:242-246`). Medium confidence.
209	- **CTE inlining (PC-5, MFS-1).** q15 scans lineitem twice in two fragments (cn1-quent.txt:990-1000: `GPU_SCAN n=56 in=122.25GB` in fragments 567 and 566, run times 2253 + 2163 ms strictly serial per cn1/cluster.log `fragment run started/finished`, agent-notes/multi-fragment-small.md section 3 (the Quent walls 4.434 / 2.149 s include the first fragment's parked wait); standalone one scan, 2627 vs 4685 ms); q11 runs the partsupp chain twice (16.4 GB + 13.1 GB). `CTEContext.needInline` (`sql/optimizer/CTEContext.java:157-190`) inlines unless cost*ratio says otherwise, and with 1-row stats inlining always wins (`cboCTERuseRatio = 1.15`, `SessionVariable.java:1511`). `SET cbo_cte_reuse_rate = 0` would force reuse (`isForceCTE`, CTEContext.java:206-217) but the CN refuses `MULTI_CAST_DATA_STREAM_SINK` by name (`compute_node_service.rs:1068`, `:1519`). This is also the plan-level cause of the q15 wrong answers (section 1).
210	- **q13 lost DENSE_COUNT_JOIN (SAJ-4).** FE plan: `5:HASH JOIN RIGHT OUTER -> 6:Project -> 7:AGGREGATE count(o_orderkey) group by c_custkey` (survey/explain/q13.costs.txt); the Substrait keeps the Project (cn1/dump/plan-0339.substrait: `aggregate -> project -> aggregate -> project -> join`); `detect_dense_count_join` (`src/planner/sirius_plan_aggregate.cpp`) requires the aggregate's direct child to be the join. Measured: CN `HASH_JOIN(6) 1.406 s + HASH_GROUP_BY(8) 0.261 s` in a 0.558 s fragment vs standalone `DENSE_COUNT_JOIN(4) 0.066 s` (cn1-ops.txt fragment 286810da3429; standalone-quent.txt); `grep -c "Fusing COUNT-join" cn1/engine-cn0.log` = 0. Proposed: look through a pure-column `LogicalProjection` in `detect_dense_count_join`, or elide the pure-subset PROJECT under an AGGREGATION_NODE in the translator. Medium confidence; it is ~0.4 s of q13's 0.38 s gap to standalone.
211	- **q20 cardinality-blind pre-aggregation and dropped runtime filters (SAJ-1).** The FE aggregates all of lineitem-1994 by `(l_partkey, l_suppkey)` before the join: exch 9 = 304,124,949 rows on 1 CN, 639,885,819 on 4 CNs (card-compare); the lineitem fragment is 3.303 s of the 3.800 s span with `MERGE_GROUP_BY(4) n=6 2.903 s` (cn1-quent.txt q20.r1); the runtime filters the FE attached to the lineitem scan (`filter_id 2/3, remote=true`, survey/explain/q20.costs.txt) are dropped. Standalone joins lineitem with the 8.69M delim keys below the aggregate (`DYNAMIC_FILTER(25)` on the scan) in 2.958 s. Proposed: implement remote runtime filters (as in P2) or, as an interim, honour the FE's STREAMING pre-aggregation mode as pass-through in `agg_phase.rs`. Medium confidence.
212	- **q07 dynamic filter no-op on the orders stream (FWJ-3).** cn1-ops.txt fragment 772c72f753ea: `DYNAMIC_FILTER(21)` on the 18.38 GB orders stream ran at +0.097 s, before its build published (Quent task timestamps), `PARTITION(22)` input 18.38 GB (no reduction), `HASH_JOIN(24) 0.753 s` vs standalone `HASH_JOIN(34) 0.072 s` with orders pre-filtered 18.37 -> 1.49 GB at the scan. On 4 CNs the planner logs `Not wiring dynamic filter(s): build side carries neither filter nor opaque-build evidence` (cn4/engine-.cn1.log 13:19:58.309). ~1.0 s of GPU operator time, ~0.25-0.3 s of wall in the join fragment. Proposed: treat a declared stream far below the base table as filter evidence (`src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664`) and add a dependency edge from the DF pipeline to the build's publish when the probe is a parked stream. Medium confidence.
213	- **The engine's in-fragment re-plan works, but only inside a fragment (PC-6).** Declared stream cardinalities equal actual parked rows for every stream (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare), DuckDB reorders inner joins with them (q19: engine built on filtered part and probed the 128.6M-row lineitem stream, cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546; q07: build/probe of three joins flipped vs the FE), but `STATISTICS_PROPAGATION` is disabled (`src/sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240`), so a FILES() scan inside the same fragment keeps its raw estimate, and the fragment cut is fixed before any of this. Also see C2.
214	- **Two-phase aggregation is cheap (AGG-5).** q01/q06 merge and result fragments 3-24 ms, hops 1-7 ms, 20-40 ms total post-scan; parity 1.04/0.97. The translator's decimal lowering shifts ~0.5 s of summed GPU time into PROJECTION and is the 9.6e-4 deviation source. Low priority.

215	
216	#### Disputed planning finding
217	
218	**PC-3: "the 4-CN BROADCAST->PARTITIONED flip is the measured source of the 0.43-0.59 scaling efficiency": refuted on the causal claim, plan facts stand.** The data skeptic's objection: the efficiency band exists without any data movement. q01 moves 0.00 GB and reaches 0.59; q06 0.00 GB, 0.56; q15 1.27 GB, 0.58; q19 2.75 GB, 0.53; against q03 60.34 GB, 0.48 and q07 69.01 GB, 0.43 (results-ratios.md, cn4-transmits.txt). Movement therefore accounts for at most ~0.05-0.15 of efficiency on the heaviest queries and none of the ~0.4 baseline loss. The baseline loss is measured elsewhere: per-GB `GPU_SCAN` Computing rises 1.3-1.6x on 4 CNs for every query including the join-free ones (q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q14 0.069 -> 0.112; cn1-quent.json vs cn4-quent.json top_ops), and ~0.2 s per query is outside the engine span on both arms (P4). Two attributions in PC-3 are also wrong: q07's dominant mover is the 1.82B-row lineitem shuffle (43.75 GB), not the 600M-row customer broadcast (3.71 GB); q02's are the four 800M-row partsupp shuffles (38.5 GB), not the 472M-row broadcast (4.25 GB). q12's orders shuffle is off the critical path (sender Computing 0.255 s overlapping the compute-bound lineitem scan). Keep the table in P3 as the plan-level fact; do not attribute the efficiency band to it.
219	
220	### 3B. Cardinality
221	
222	#### C1 (confirmed). Every FE estimate is 1 row; actuals reach 6.0e9
223	
224	**Measured.** `card_all_one=True` for all 22 plans (survey/plan-summary.txt). Exchanges carrying >= 100M rows on 1 CN (card-compare-cn1.txt, last line): q02/exch3 800M, q02/exch28 800M, q02/exch34 118M, q02/exch36 118M, q03/exch8 146M, q04/exch4 3,793M, q05/exch1 150M, q05/exch4 228M, q07/exch8 1,823M, q07/exch12 1,500M, q07/exch16 150M, q10/exch12 115M, q13/exch2 1,484M, q13/exch4 150M, q14/exch3 200M, q19/exch3 129M, q20/exch9 304M, q20/exch12 800M, q21/exch6 731M, q22/exch10 1,500M. On 4 CNs (card-compare-cn4.txt) the list grows to 26 entries and the summed broadcast rows reach 6,000M (q22/exch10).
225	
226	**Source.** `StatisticsCalculator.java:664-676` (quoted in P1). Reached for FILES() via `visitLogicalTableFunctionTableScan` (:374-375). Consequences confirmed in source: `checkBroadcastRowCountLimit` inert (P3); CTE inlining always wins (P5); `JoinCommutativityRule` never commutes semi/anti (P5); the translator comment at `node_translator.rs:1918-1929` already records that "the FE reports cardinality: 1 for every FILES() external scan" and that "bounding it belongs to the executor".
227	
228	**Where row counts already exist.** (a) FE-only, no wire change: `TableFunctionTable.parseFilesForLoadAndQuery` records every file's byte size (`catalog/TableFunctionTable.java:611 brokerFileStatus.setSize(fileStatus.getLen())`, exposed via `loadFileList()` :300); `computeFileScanNode` can estimate rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema. (b) Exact: `file_schema.rs:19-27` already opens every footer (`ParquetRecordBatchStreamBuilder` metadata) for the schema RPC; `FileMetaData.num_rows` is available but `PGetFileSchemaResult` carries only status + schema (`gensrc/proto/internal_service.proto:647-650`), so this is a proto + FE + CN change, not FE-only. (c) Later: per-column min/max from row-group stats for the date range predicates.
229	
230	**Limits (inference, from the FE estimator code).** Row counts without column statistics leave `ColumnStatistic.unknown()` in place: range predicates on unknown columns cost 0.5 (`BinaryPredicateStatisticCalculator.estimatePredicateRange` -> `OVERLAP_INFINITE_RANGE_FILTER_COEFFICIENT`), IN 0.5, string equality 1.0, and join output = `max(L, R)` (`StatisticsCalculator.computeJoinNode :1219-1240`). That separates lineitem from nation and orders from region, which is what the fragment cut needs most, but it also arms the broadcast guard against mid-sized broadcasts (P3) and gives no NDV for the aggregate outputs that decide q02's join 37. Verify with `EXPLAIN COSTS` on q05/q22/q03 after the change; this was not run.
231	
232	Confidence: high on the defect; medium-high on fix (a); the predicted plan outcomes are inference.
233	
234	#### C2 (confirmed). The receiver-first exact cardinality mechanism is correct but arrives too late and is undermined by a flat 0.2 selectivity on the FE's `IS NOT NULL` conjunct
235	
236	**Measured.** `engine.rs:551-590` sums parked `output_row_count` over local senders and remote batch rows and calls `declare_input_cardinality` before `build()`; `src/include/exec/stream_bind_catalog.hpp:42-47` feeds it to DuckDB's TableFunction cardinality callback. Every declared count equals the actual parked rows (cn1-cnlog.txt `cards[]` vs card-compare-cn1.txt). It only helps inside a fragment: q19's engine plan builds on the filtered part and probes the stream (cn1-ops.txt 6493-6546: `STREAMING_SOURCE(4)->DYNAMIC_FILTER(5)` 3.66 GB -> 0.01 GB, fragment 150 ms) although the FE made lineitem the build.
237	
238	**BJ-4 (not adversarially verified, medium confidence).** In q10 the receiver builds on the 150M-row, 25.5 GB customer x nation side instead of the 114.7M-row, 2.29 GB stream (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573: `PARTITION(8) 25.55 GB 0.479 s, CONCAT(9) 0.114 s, HASH_JOIN(14) 0.301 s`; the stream is behind `DYNAMIC_FILTER(11)`, i.e. probe). The translated plan carries `Filter[is_not_null($0)](customer Read)` from the FE's null-rejecting scan conjunct (`expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`), and DuckDB applies `DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY = 0.2` to it (`duckdb/src/include/duckdb/optimizer/join_order/relation_statistics_helper.hpp:57`), so 150M x 0.2 = 30M < 114.7M declared. Standalone has no such filter and estimates customer x nation at 151.5M. The 0.2 arithmetic is inferred from source, not from a printed estimate. Proposed (translator, `experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator/src/expr_translator.rs:630/929 is_not_null_pred`; medium confidence): do not emit the FE's join-key `IS NOT NULL` conjunct as a Filter rel (the join drops nulls anyway), or attach it to the ReadRel as a table filter. Measured stake: the `PARTITION(8) + CONCAT(9) + HASH_JOIN(14)` chain is 0.89 s of summed GPU time in q10's 1067 ms receiver fragment (cn1-ops.txt 3437-3573).
239	
240	#### C3 (confirmed, one correction). The engine's own reservation estimate is exact once a pipeline has history, but the cold-start estimate is 8x, and four cold-start scan tasks reserve 58-80% of the pool
241	
242	**Measured** (agent-notes/req_hist.py, raw Quent Reserving records). q01: after the first task completes, each scan task requests exactly its measured peak (6.98 GB for a 2.41 GB input, 2.9x); the first 4 tasks of every scan pipeline request 19.52 GB each (histogram `{8.1: 4, 2.9: 103}`). q06: 13.32 GB x 4 then 3.74 GB. Source: `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:66 kMaxNumericCarrierExpansion = 8`, `:648-668 no_history_peak_memory_estimate` = bytes x 8 + filter working set; `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:872-880` takes the no-history branch for every task dispatched before the first completion. Max concurrent reservation held by the 4 slots (agent-notes/bj6_sweep.py): q03 79.6 GiB, q10 75.9, q12 79.7, q14 67.7, q19 58.0 on cn1; the same per CN on cn4 and in standalone. Reservations are charged to the same counter as live allocations (`cucascade/src/memory/reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`), and the engine's `[gpu_pool]` running peak reached 99.16 GB (92%) inside q03.r0's lineitem fragment and 106.09 GB (98.8%) in q04.r0 (cn1/engine-cn0.log windows 51 and 65).
243	
244	Summed request vs summed peak (reservation-ratio.txt): cn1 q11 236.2 GB vs 4.3 GB (54x), q14 15.2x, q03 14.2x, q10 6.3x; cn4 q11 67.7x; standalone q13 549.8 GB vs 0.9 GB (611x, DENSE_COUNT_JOIN path), q14 68x. On 4 CNs every CN pays the 4-task wave per fragment, which is the whole of the higher 1.27/1.64 ratios for q01/q06.
245	
246	**Join/receiver fragments over-reserve through a different path (measured, mechanism not investigated).** The scan cold-start rule above does not explain the receiver fragments: cn1 q04.r1 F00 (orders scan + RIGHT_SEMI join over the 30.8 GB lineitem stream, 151 tasks) requested 253.1 GB for a 61.3 GB summed peak (4.1x; cn1-quent.txt q04.r1 fragment `...8480`), q07.r1 F08 (217 tasks, four joins) 163.1 GB for 26.3 GB (6.2x; fragment `...753ea`), q13.r1 F04 100.7 GB for 43.8 GB (2.3x). Reserving time in these fragments is 0.002-0.043 s, so the over-estimate did not block them at the 100 GiB pool; it would at a smaller pool or more slots. The operator-level estimates (hash join / partition / concat) were not read for this report; listed in section 5.
247	
248	**Correction to BJ-6.** The gate did trip at 1 CN: every Reserving > 10 ms in q10/q12/q14 ends exactly when another task releases (agent-notes/refute-bj6/slow_reserving.py: q10 r0/r1/r2 177.1/177.7/174.4 ms for a 20.4 GB request while 3 tasks held 61.1 GB plus 31.6 GB of leaked parked data, finding B4; q12 108.6 + 47.0 ms; q14 128-139 ms), reproducibly in all three runs, 0 at 4 CNs and in standalone. `memory_space::make_reservation` blocks on a notification channel until a release (`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`, `notification_channel.cpp:47-59`). # OOM-5 refutation check (post-failure parked-output leak)

Files produced here: cn-events.txt (ANSI-stripped CN events from cn1/cluster.log with line numbers),
pool-trace.txt (engine-cn0.log [gpu_pool] QueryBegin/End 13:02-13:19:30, GB), headroom.txt (per run: baseline at
start, max allocated at any fragment boundary, own peak, headroom to the 107.37 GB cap).

## Mechanism: CONFIRMED (code + logs)
- compute_node_service.rs:449-478 cancel_plan_fragment only calls results.cancel(); comment says real teardown is a
  separate work item. run_ready_fragment (:862-905) on receiver failure calls results.fail_query() only; no parked drop,
  no per-query skip. engine.rs:278-300: engine thread serves Run requests one at a time; parked/parked_slots are cleared
  only when run_fragment returns Err (process-wide wipe).
- cluster.log: after every `fragment run failed` the not-yet-run senders of the same query still start and finish:
  q05 (13:05:24.632-25.355: ..5773, ..5777, ..5776, ..5775 [inputs=2, drains streams 1 and 4]), q08 (13:08:29.792-30.836),
  q09 (13:12:22.333-22.721: ..947 ..946 ..945 ..944), q17 (13:14:56.819-13:15:03.233: two senders, one 6343 ms),
  q21 (13:18:07.604-10.954: two fragments, one inputs=1 draining stream 6 = 730,806,711 rows, 3153 ms), q18: none left.
- q16 (translator error at 13:13:12.910) ran two senders BEFORE the failure (ff87 partsupp 6.6 GB, ff86 supplier); the
  failure never went through run_fragment Err so they were not wiped (dump fragment-0421/-0422 identify the tables).

# Fix 2, robust design: query-scoped teardown of parked output on the CN

Angle: the design a senior engineer ships for the long run. Correct under cancellation and

## 0. Summary

Today a query's parked sender output on a CN is released only by the receiver that consumes it.
When the query dies, three things go wrong (all measured on the 1-CN SF1000 sweep):

1. The engine thread's `Err` path wipes **every** parked output process-wide
   (`engine.rs:291-316`), which is collateral damage for any concurrent query and does not even
   help the failing one on 1 CN (see 4.1).
2. The dead query's not-yet-run senders keep running and park output nobody will consume
   (`dispatch_worker` has no notion of a dead query, `compute_node_service.rs:380-390`):
   0-36.64 GB leaked per failure, 0.39-6.42 s of engine-thread time stolen from the next query.
3. `cancel_plan_fragment` touches only the result store (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476`), and
   a failure that never enters the engine (translation, q16) drops nothing.

The design replaces the process-wide wipe with **one query-scoped teardown**,
`ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)`, reachable from three triggers (a fragment
failure, an FE cancel, a TTL sweep) and acting on four subsystems (the engine's parked
registry, the dispatch path, the exchange rendezvous, the result store). Teardown is idempotent,
tolerates the transport's late `drop_parked`, refuses late `Run`s of the dead query at two gates,
logs one structured report per teardown, and has two knobs. It changes nothing on the hot path of
a healthy query beyond a hash lookup per fragment run.

Predicted effect on the SF1000 1-CN sweep: the six post-failure leaks (4.69 / 8.83 / 31.56 /
+6.60 / 4.00 / 36.64 GB) become 0; the ~11.9 s of leftover-sender time (q05->q06 0.72,
q08->q09 1.04, q09->q10 0.39, q17->q18 6.42, q21->q22 3.35 s) disappears; q22 cold drops from
4110 ms to about 1.0-1.2 s; the 15 passing queries are unchanged (their QUERY_FINISHED cancels
tear down an empty registry).

## 3. The design

### 3.1 One entry point, three triggers, four subsystems

```
trigger                     ServiceCore::terminate_query(query_id, cause)      subsystem action
------------------------    -------------------------------------------      --------------------------------
run_ready_fragment Err  ->  1. lifecycle.mark(query_id, cause)          ->  dispatch gate: later Runs skipped
process_fragment Err        2. executor.terminate_query(query_id,cause) ->  engine: mark + DropQuery (async)
cancel_plan_fragment    ->  3. exchanges.remove_query(query_id)         ->  rendezvous purged; staged leases
   (INTERNAL_ERROR,            + remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)         released via staging_release
    TIMEOUT, USER_CANCEL)   4. results.fail_query / nothing              ->  FE-polled ids fail (or untouched)
cancel_plan_fragment    ->  same, with cause = Finished (release-only)
   (QUERY_FINISHED,
    LIMIT_REACH)
TTL sweep (engine)      ->  engine-local drop_query + warn; CN lifecycle learns it on next touch
```

`TerminationCause` is an enum, not a string: `Failed { fragment: FragmentInstanceId, error }`,
`Cancelled { reason: PPlanFragmentCancelReason, message: Option<String> }`,
`Finished { reason }` (QUERY_FINISHED / LIMIT_REACH), `Expired { idle: Duration }`. `Display`
renders the text that today's `missing_slot` (`engine.rs:369-377`) and the FE error carry.

### 3.2 Engine thread: `ParkedRegistry`, a terminated set, two gates

```rust
    let first = self.lifecycle.mark(query_id, cause.clone());
    if let Err(err) = self.executor.terminate_query(query_id, cause.clone()) { error!(...) }   // engine is authoritative for GPU bytes
    let purged = self.exchanges.remove_query(query_id);                                          // receivers registered for q + their sources
    let purged_instances: Vec<_> = finst_ids.iter().flat_map(|id| self.exchanges.remove_receiver_instance(*id)).collect();
    for source in purged.sources.into_iter().chain(purged_instances) {
        match source {
            SenderSource::LocalParked { slot, .. } => { /* engine drop_query covers it; nothing to do */ }
            SenderSource::Remote { batches, .. } => for b in batches.iter().filter(|b| b.len > 0) {
                if let Err(err) = self.executor.staging_release(b.offset) { warn!(offset = b.offset, %err, "failed to release a staged lease of a terminated query") }
            }
        }
    }
    match &*cause {
        TerminationCause::Failed { fragment, error } => self.results.fail_query(query_id, *fragment, error.clone()),
        TerminationCause::Cancelled { message, .. } => self.results.fail_query_all(query_id, cause.to_string()),   // new: fail every reserved result id, record query_failures
        TerminationCause::Finished { .. } | TerminationCause::Expired { .. } => {}                                // release-only
    }
    if first { info!(query_id, trigger = %cause.trigger(), receivers = purged.receivers, remote_sources = .., staged_leases = .., "query teardown") }
}
```

Call sites:

1. `run_ready_fragment` `Err` arm (`:875-909`): replace `self.results.fail_query(...)` with
   `self.terminate_query(query_id, Failed{fragment: id, error}, &[])`. Covers engine failures
   (also already marked by the engine), translation failures with slots in hand (q16 -- the
   engine's `drop_query` releases them), remote drain failures (`join_into_ready`), rendezvous
   errors.
2. `exec_single_attachment` / `translate_batch_attachment` `Err` (the inline RPC path,
   `:705-720, 1624+`): when `process_fragment` fails for a fragment that carries a query id,
   call `terminate_query` before returning the error to the FE. Any RPC error fails the query on
   the FE (`FragmentInstanceExecState.waitForDeploymentCompletion`, seen at `cluster.log` 6186),
   so marking is never premature. Survey mode (`SIRIUS_CN_TRANSLATE_ONLY`) returns Ok and is
   unaffected.
3. `cancel_plan_fragment` (`:457-482`): see 3.6.

### 3.5 Dispatch gates on the CN side

- `run_ready_fragment` start: `if let Some(cause) = self.lifecycle.check(query_id) { info!(query_id, fragment_instance_id, %cause, "skipping fragment of a terminated query"); return Vec::new(); }`.
  This is what removes the leftover senders in async mode (they sit in the worker's inbox).
- `run_labeled` (`:1540-1581`), just before `self.executor.run(run)`: the same check, so a
  sender running inline in its RPC (default mode) is refused with
  `Err("fragment of terminated query ...")` instead of touching the engine. RPC threads already
  blocked in `engine_call` are caught by engine GATE 1.
- `process_fragment` for a **new** fragment of a terminated query (the FE's deploy of a late
  level racing its own cancel): refuse with the cause. The FE ignores the error (its
  `queryStatus` is already non-OK, `DefaultCoordinator.java:1056-1058`).

### 3.6 Cancel semantics by reason

| `cancel_reason` | FE meaning | CN action |
|---|---|---|
| 3 INTERNAL_ERROR, 4 TIMEOUT, 2 USER_CANCEL | query is dead; `error_message` set for 3 | `terminate_query(q, Cancelled{reason, message}, &[finst_id])`; result store: `fail_query_all` with the FE's message (keeps today's "cancelled by the FE: {message}" text that the test at `:3414-3460` pins) |
| 5 QUERY_FINISHED, 1 LIMIT_REACH | FE has all rows | `terminate_query(q, Finished{reason}, &[finst_id])`: release-only. Result store untouched (a `Pending` entry the FE has not drained must not be failed). Optional, separate commit: evict `Drained` entries and the query's `descriptor_tables` cache entry (`:985`; result_store.rs TODO `:250-254`) |
| none / unknown | old FE | treat as INTERNAL_ERROR without a message |
| `finst_id == (0,0)` | phased-schedule query-level cancel (`ExecutionDAG.cancelQueryContext`) | same path keyed by `query_id` only |
| `query_id` absent | pre-field FE | `results.cancel(finst_id)` + `exchanges.remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)` only (today's behaviour plus the purge) |

The handler still returns OK immediately: everything it calls is a mutex insert, a channel send,
or a rendezvous map operation; `staging_release` is the arena's own mutex (`engine.rs:793-811`).
Knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL=0` reduces cancel to today's result-store mark (escape hatch
if a StarRocks version ever sends cancels for live queries).

### 3.7 Rendezvous: `LocalExchange::remove_query` / `remove_receiver_instance`

`local_exchange.rs`: `PendingReceiver` gains `query_id: Option<QueryId>` (from
`params.params.query_id`, computed by the caller and passed to `register_receiver`);
`push_sender` gains a `query_id` argument (the sender's own, available at
`compute_node_service.rs:1193-1203`) recorded in `receiver_query: HashMap<FragmentInstanceId, QueryId>`.
Remote frames carry no query id on the wire (`internal_service.proto:812-827`), and none is
needed: the FE deploys receiver-first and waits for the level's replies before deploying senders
(`Deployer`, report P4), so the receiver is registered before its first frame; and every cancel
names the instance, so `remove_receiver_instance(finst_id)` purges any orphan `sources` entry
without a query mapping. `take_ready` keeps its removals; `remote_seq` is purged alongside.

```rust
pub(crate) struct PurgedRendezvous { pub receivers: usize, pub sources: Vec<SenderSource> }
pub(crate) fn remove_query(&self, query_id: QueryId) -> PurgedRendezvous;
pub(crate) fn remove_receiver_instance(&self, id: FragmentInstanceId) -> Vec<SenderSource>;
```

### 3.8 Sweep: the safety net for a silent FE

A `std::thread` timer posts `EngineRequest::Sweep` every `min(ttl/4, 60 s)`; the engine thread
drops parked output whose query has had no touch (park, relay, export, frame) for
`SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` (default 1800; 0 disables) and warns once at `ttl/2`. The TTL must
exceed the FE's `query_timeout` (300 s default) by a wide margin because a receiver legitimately
waits for the slowest sender of its query. The sweep is the only path that frees memory when the
FE dies without cancelling, and it also prunes `torn_down`/`terminated` retention
(`SIRIUS_CN_TERMINATED_RETAIN_SECS`, default 600, bounded so a late deploy of a dead query is still
refused). Knobs go through `tunable.rs` (`Knob` with name/default/min/max, reject-not-clamp,
logged at bring-up; `tunable.rs:1-60`).

### 3.9 Observability

- One `query teardown` line per (query, trigger) at INFO when nothing was parked, WARN when
  something was: `query_id trigger=engine_err|cn_err|cancel:<reason>|finished|sweep slots
  fragments batches rows oldest_parked_ms receivers_purged staged_leases_released skipped_runs`.
  Rows/batches come from `Fragment::output_row_count` / `output_batch_count`
  (`rust/crates/sirius/src/lib.rs:375-386`) with `.ok()` (a spilled batch throws,
  `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066`, same tolerance as `engine.rs:559-566`).
- `skipping fragment of a terminated query` at INFO with the cause: this is the line the SF1000
  acceptance test greps for absence of `fragment run started` after `fragment run failed`.
- The engine-thread `fragment` span (`engine.rs:440-451`) records `parked_queries` and
  `parked_slots` at entry, so every run's close event carries the standing inventory; the sweep
  logs the inventory at INFO. Bytes stay where they are measured today: the engine's
  `[gpu_pool] QueryBegin/QueryEnd allocated=` lines (`src/sirius_context.cpp:271`).
- Optional (engine `src/` follow-up, not required): `Fragment::output_bytes(stream)` so the
  teardown line can carry bytes.

## 4. Behaviour under the measured cases

### 4.1 The 1-CN SF1000 sweep, failure by failure

The process-wide wipe was **not** the leak on 1 CN: at every wipe only the failing query's own
slots were parked (one query at a time), so today's `parked.clear()` and the new `drop_query`
free the same bytes. What changes is what happens next:

| transition | today (measured) | with the design |
|---|---|---|
| q05 -> q06 | 5773/5777/5776/5775 run 13:05:24.632-25.355 (0.72 s), 5775 relays streams 1+4 and parks 4.69 GB that survives q06/q07 | engine `Err` at 13:05:24.626 marks q05 terminated on the engine thread; `run_ready_fragment` marks it on the CN and the worker's next pop (5773) is skipped with `skipping fragment of a terminated query`; 5777/5776/5775 likewise; the 11 cancels at .632 find q05 already torn down (idempotent). q06 starts at once; pool at q06 QueryBegin = 0.00 GB |
| q08 -> q09 | 6 leftovers 13:08:29.792-30.680 (1.04 s), 8.83 GB into q09 | skipped; 0 GB; q09's lineitem sender starts with a clean pool |
| q09 -> q10..q16 | 4 leftovers (0.39 s), 31.56 GB parked through 7 queries (21 runs); 47-178 ms reservation-gate blocks in q10/q12/q14 | skipped; 0 GB; the gate blocks in C3 lose their cause (**inference**: up to 0.18 s per q10/q12/q14 warm run recovered) |
| q16 (translation failure of receiver ff85) | senders ff86/ff87 parked 6.6 GB never dropped (no engine `Err`); +6.6 GB into q17 | `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query(q16, Failed)` -> engine `DropQuery` frees ff86/ff87 within the same millisecond (engine idle) |
| q17 -> q18 | aca2 + aca1 (6.34 s scan) run after the failure, 4.0 GB into q18 | skipped: q18's timer starts 13:14:56.823 and its first fragment can start at ~.83 instead of 13:15:03.243 (6.42 s earlier) |
| q21 -> q22 | 2acc + 2acb (3.15 s, parks 36.64 GB) run after the failure; q22 cold 4110 ms, warm runs carry 36.64 GB | skipped; q22 cold = its own 0.755 s of fragments + FE head (~0.2 s, P4) + first-touch: predicted 1.0-1.2 s; warm 943 ms unchanged |

Note the 0.25 ms race in q05: sender 5773 started **before** the first cancel ack. The design
does not depend on cancel for this; the CN marks the query at `run_ready_fragment`'s `Err`, which
executes on the dispatch worker *before* it pops 5773. In default (inline) mode the same senders
are RPC threads blocked in `engine_call`; engine GATE 1 refuses them because the engine thread
marked the query at its own `Err` before responding.

### 4.2 The 15 passing queries (1 CN and 4 CN)

Per fragment run: one `HashMap` lookup in `run_ready_fragment`/`run_labeled`, one in engine
GATE 1, one in GATE 2, one `by_query` insert on park. Per query: 2-13 QUERY_FINISHED cancels
(`cn1-cnlog.txt cancels=`), each a `terminate_query(Finished)` that finds an empty registry
(every parked output was consumed before the result fragment could run, by construction of the
receiver-first rendezvous, B1) and logs at INFO. On 4 CNs a QUERY_FINISHED cancel can arrive on a
sender CN while the transport thread has transmitted eos but not yet called `drop_parked`
(`nixl_transport.rs:774-790`); `release` returns `AlreadyTornDown` and the drain reports success.
No plan, memory, or ordering change for these queries; warm medians should be within noise
(compare.py set unchanged).

### 4.3 Cases the campaign did not exercise

- **User `KILL` mid-run** (USER_CANCEL while the engine is inside the query's fragment): cancel
  marks + posts `DropQuery`; the running fragment cannot be aborted (engine limitation, B3), but
  GATE 2 drops its output instead of parking, the CN never registers it, and every other fragment
  of the query is skipped. Memory returns as soon as the fragment ends.
- **Failure on another CN**: that CN's `run_ready_fragment` `Err` -> `fail_query` there; FE
  cancels every instance everywhere with INTERNAL_ERROR; this CN's parked output for the query
  (waiting on a drain, or already drained but the peer receiver died) is dropped by the cancel;
  an in-flight drain's next `export` fails with the teardown cause; staged remote frames for a
  receiver of the dead query on this CN are purged and their leases released (today they pin the
  arena forever, B6-adjacent).
- **FE dies, no cancel**: the sweep frees the output after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` and warns
  at half that; `parked_inventory` shows what is waiting.
- **Late deploy of a dead query** (FE level in flight when the failure happened): refused at
  `process_fragment` while the retention entry lives (600 s); after retention, it would register
  a receiver that never completes and be swept by the TTL.

## 5. Failure modes of the design itself

| # | scenario | what happens | why acceptable |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | QUERY_FINISHED cancel races the transport's post-eos `drop_parked` | `release` -> `AlreadyTornDown` (Ok) | test 7.5; without it a finished query's sender RPC would report an error |
| F2 | INTERNAL_ERROR cancel during an in-flight drain | next `export_packed_next` -> `Err(TornDown cause)`; drain fails; sender RPC / `fail_query` reports the teardown cause, not "no parked sender output" | the query is dead; the message names the culprit (the q08 lesson) |
| F3 | `terminate_query` for a query with a fragment mid-run on the engine | cannot abort; output dropped at GATE 2 when it ends | documented limitation; engine abort is fix-1/B3 territory |
| F4 | FE never sends cancel (crash) | TTL sweep frees after `SIRIUS_CN_PARKED_TTL_SECS` | default 1800 s >> FE query_timeout 300 s; knob |
| F5 | TTL too low for a legitimately long query (many-minute sender at SF10000) | its receiver fails with "sender output ... expired after N s" | loud, names the knob; warn at ttl/2 gives operators a signal first |
| F6 | Two failures of the same query (engine `Err` then CN `Err` then cancel) | `mark` keeps the first cause; later triggers log at DEBUG with `already_terminated=true` | idempotent by construction |
| F7 | Query id absent on the run (translate-only fixtures) | parked under `None`; only an `Err` of a `None` run drops the `None` bucket; never swept by query | preserves today's semantics for anonymous fragments |
| F8 | `DropQuery` posted while the engine is shutting down | `send_nowait` returns Err, logged; `Drop for SiriusEngine` drops the registry with the context (`engine.rs:359-361`) | nothing leaks past process exit |
| F9 | `staging_release` of a purged remote batch fails (arena gone) | warned, teardown continues | same tolerance as `engine.rs:470-476` |
| F10 | `terminated`/`torn_down`/`lifecycle` growth | bounded by retention (600 s) and by the sweep | one entry per query, pruned |
| F11 | A CN with async dispatch OFF and a sender RPC that failed at `route_destination` before running | `process_fragment` `Err` -> `terminate_query` | consistent: the FE fails the query on any RPC error |
| F12 | Knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL=0` | cancel reverts to `results.cancel`; Err-time and sweep paths still active | escape hatch only for the cancel contract |

## 10. Risks

1. **Cancel contract drift.** The design assumes StarRocks sends QUERY_FINISHED only after the FE
   has every row (`DefaultCoordinator.java:1022-1035`). It does, and the CN's single-batch model
   means all parked output is consumed by then; the knob `SIRIUS_CN_TEARDOWN_ON_CANCEL` is the
   escape hatch. Mitigation: test 7.2.6/7.2.8 and the 4-CN smoke assertion `slots=0` on finished
   teardowns.
2. **Refusing a fragment the FE still expects.** `process_fragment` refusal of a late deploy of a
   terminated query returns an RPC error to an FE that has already failed the query -- harmless.
   If retention were shorter than the FE's deploy window the late fragment would register and be
   swept by the TTL instead; 600 s is far above any deploy.
3. **GATE 2 discards work.** Output of a fragment that finished after its query was terminated is
   dropped rather than parked; that is the intent, but a mis-marked query (a bug in a trigger)
   would lose a live query's output loudly ("terminated while running"). First-cause-wins and
   the cause text make such a bug diagnosable in one log line.
4. **TTL misconfiguration** (F5) can fail a long-running legitimate query; the default is 6x the
   FE query timeout and the warn-at-half gives a signal first. Set to 0 to disable in bring-up
   experiments.
5. **Engine backlog.** `DropQuery` is FIFO behind whatever the engine thread is doing; for a
   cancel during a 100 s fragment of the same query, the release happens when that fragment ends
   (F3). No new blocking anywhere.
6. **Interaction with fix 4(b) (spillable parked repositories).** If parked repositories get
   registered with the downgrade executor, dropping a `Fragment` must unregister them; flag to
   that design. Row counting already tolerates a spilled batch (`.ok()`).
7. **Behavioural change for the inline sender path**: a queued sender of a dead query now returns
   an RPC error instead of running; the FE already treats the query as failed, and
   `dispatched_receiver_failure_surfaces_through_fetch_data`-style tests cover the surfaced text.

1. **Registry + Err-time per-query drop** (`parked.rs`, `engine.rs`, `fragment_executor.rs`
   trait defaults, unit tests 7.1 + GPU tests 7.3): pure hygiene, no dispatch-contract change.
   ~1 day.
2. **Query lifecycle: terminate on Err and cancel, dispatch gates, rendezvous purge, idempotent
   release** (`compute_node_service.rs`, `local_exchange.rs`, `result_store.rs`, tests 7.2):
   touches the dispatch contract; this is the PR that fixes the measured leak. ~1.5 days.
3. **Sweep, retention, knobs, telemetry fields, docs** (`tunable.rs`, sweep thread, span fields,
   `TUNABLES.md`, `DEMO.md`, `cnlog_extract.py`): ~1 day.

SF1000 verification: one 1-CN sweep in campaign order (~16 min of GPU time with today's
54-232 s failures; ~4 min if fix 1 is already in) plus a 4-CN 15-query smoke. Total 3.5-4
engineer-days.

## 12. Dependencies and interactions with the other three fixes

- **Fix 1 (fail fast in the reschedule loop, engine `src/`)**: independent code. Ordering: land
  fix 2 first or together; with fix 1 alone the leftover-sender time becomes the dominant part of
  each failure's wall (q17: 3 s to fail, 6.4 s of leftovers). Fix 1's new error text lands in
  `TerminationCause::Failed { error }` and is what the teardown line and the FE message carry.
- **Fix 3 (FE cardinalities)**: no interaction; fewer failures means fewer teardowns.
- **Fix 4(a) (fragment fusion)**: fused fragments are ordinary runs; fewer exchanges, fewer parked
  outputs; no interaction. **Fix 4(b) (spillable parked repositories)**: `Fragment` drop must
  unregister from the downgrade registry (risk 6); `DropReport.rows` stays optional because
  `output_row_count` throws on a spilled batch until 4(b) adds host-side counts.
- No dependency on a proto or FE change; the FE already sends everything the design consumes.

On 1 CN the wipe itself was not the leak (only the failing query's slots were parked); the leftover runs are. Design: (1) engine.rs maps -> ParkedRegistry<F> in parked.rs with ParkedOutput{query_id,...}, torn_down map replacing `poisoned`, drop_query(query)->DropReport, release() returning Ok(AlreadyTornDown) for torn-down slots (transport's post-eos drop_parked stays correct), get_mut() -> Err naming the teardown cause; a shared Arc<Mutex<HashMap<QueryId,cause>>> `terminated` checked at Run dequeue (GATE 1) and again before park (GATE 2, drops output of a fragment whose query died mid-run); Err marks the query on the engine thread itself.
